structural: The text of `requirements.sdk.graph.search.search_text.behavior` has no structural obligations. It has no implementation roots, and none are needed.

I checked each clause for an alternative implementation that keeps the observable behavior but violates the clause:

- **"The harness groups matching occurrences under `group_hits` and renders each excerpt under `windows`."** This only points to other requirements through {cite}. It names no library, algorithm, type or interface. Any grouping or windowing code that gives the same results satisfies it. Those requirements carry their own text and are judged separately.
- **"Each entry's `node` is a reference under `node_reference`."** This describes the output value: a node ID in the shape that requirement defines. Returning the same ID from any code path is indistinguishable. The ID's representation and the address resolution belong to `requirements.sdk.graph.validation-context.node_reference`.
- **"`complete` reports whether the search exhausted its scope."** This is the meaning of an output field, which is observable behavior. The field name is part of the tool's output. Changing it would change the tool's output, not just the implementation. How the flag is computed is discretionary.

All clauses specify observable behavior or delegate to cited requirements, so no `{impl}` marker is required. `outgoing_edges` with label `Implements` on node 2573 returned no targets, which is consistent with this.

behavioral: The subject adds no new behavior of its own. It requires that the harness's text search group hits under `requirements.sdk.graph.search.group_hits`, render excerpts under `requirements.sdk.graph.search.windows`, and give each entry a `node` under `requirements.sdk.graph.validation-context.node_reference`. It also requires that `complete` report whether the search exhausted its scope. The four marked tests cover these in the subject's own case:

- **Grouping, merged windows and clipping.** `search_groups_exact_occurrences_and_records_the_selected_declaration` in `crates/trust-but-verify/src/agent/project_sources.rs` searches `éhit` and `hit hit` across two consts. `TextMatches` has one hit per occurrence (3 hits with exact spans). The agent tool returns exactly two entries, one for `const[A]` and one for `const[B]`. The two hits in `const[B]` give a single entry whose excerpt is the contiguous source `const B: &str = "hit hit";`. This shows the overlapping windows are emitted once, the text between the hits is kept, and the window is clipped to the item span. The multibyte `é` is retained.
- **Node references.** The same test asserts each entry's `node` equals the interned `code.rs#const[A]` or `code.rs#const[B]`, with sequential tags. `search_obligations_follow_delivery_and_keep_the_original_snapshot` asserts that a later page's `node` equals the interned domain node for its selector. It also asserts that distinct tags are issued per page and that finishing a tag records the dependency on the selected item.
- **`complete`.** `search_obligations_follow_delivery_and_keep_the_original_snapshot` asserts `complete == true` for an uncapped search and `complete == false` for `limit:1` on a source with many hits. `scoped_text_results_keep_line_numbers_context_and_completeness` in `crates/trust-but-verify/tests/source_defaults.rs` checks `complete` for unbounded, limited and scoped searches. `gitignore_is_shared_by_all_operations_with_or_without_a_git_repository` in the same file asserts `complete` for the full scan and for excluded scopes.
- **Pagination.** `search_obligations_follow_delivery_and_keep_the_original_snapshot` also covers a multi-entry first page plus a following page. Each entry's excerpt is delivered whole, and the next page is read from the original snapshot.

The detailed window rules are obligations of `requirements.sdk.graph.search.windows`, and the entry-shape rules are obligations of `requirements.sdk.graph.search.group_hits`. They are tested under those requirements by tests such as `default_windows_retain_128_bytes_on_each_side`, `root_hits_clip_context_to_utf8_boundaries` and `separated_hit_windows_preserve_the_function_declaration`. Those tests also exercise non-default `window_bytes`, so I did not reassess them here. The marked tests cover the subject's own combined behavior, and I found no unrelated missing obligation.

text: The harness groups matching occurrences under {cite}`requirements.sdk.graph.search.group_hits` and renders each excerpt under {cite}`requirements.sdk.graph.search.windows`. Each entry's `node` is a reference under {cite}`requirements.sdk.graph.validation-context.node_reference`. `complete` reports whether the search exhausted its scope.

Deliver one entry per enclosing item in a text search, even when the item has several hits. Group before pagination so an item's excerpt stays together. Each entry carries a node reference under {cite}`requirements.sdk.graph.validation-context.node_reference`, one excerpt, and the page-local tag used by `finish_search`. The tag accounts for use of the excerpt. The node reference lets the agent read the full item.

The agent's `search_text` tool accepts a nonnegative `window_bytes`, defaulting to 128. For a hit with byte span `[start, end)`, retain the hit and up to `window_bytes` of source immediately before `start` and after `end`. Clip the window to the enclosing item's span. Move a context boundary that splits a UTF-8 character inward to the nearest character boundary. With `window_bytes: 0`, only the hit spans and the available header and trailer contribute source to the excerpt.

Compute windows for all hits in the item from the same snapshot. Where windows touch or overlap, emit the contiguous source once. This preserves each hit and the text between nearby hits, including whitespace and newlines.

The harness represents a `NodeId<D>` as an unsigned integer. Each built-in tool that accepts a node accepts the same top-level address fields, alongside its own arguments (such as an edge `label`). `NodeAddress` in tool signatures denotes these alternatives:
| `node` | Look up the assigned ID in the domain's cache. |

| `path`, optional `location` | Resolve the project-relative file within the domain's visible sources. `location` is its outline selector and defaults to the empty selector for the file root. Resolve the item, map its `OutlineData` through `Domain::source_node`, and intern the resulting identity. |
| `data` | Deserialize the JSON value as `D::NodeData` and intern it in the domain's cache. |

For domains using the agent harness, the tool schema describes `data` using the domain’s JSON schema for `D::NodeData`. The harness uses the same JSON representation when returning and accepting an identity.

Resolving an address is discovery. The requested operation determines which observations enter evidence. Invalid addresses, unavailable files, and unknown selectors produce tool errors before the requested operation runs.
